result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers commit to a capped free allowance and correctly point out that a $10 starter plan can't include 500 pages. B states the full $20,000/month exposure and gives a correct, clearly labeled break-even analysis (about 9% first-month conversion, about 1.5% over six months). A covers abuse better, with repeat accounts, disposable emails and verification, while B never addresses repeat signups. B's sizing and its signals for adjusting the offer are stronger overall, so it edges ahead. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick a capped one-time credit and give concrete allowances, and both say what to track. A sizes the forever-free exposure most clearly ($10 per user per month, up to $20,000 a month), and B says only 'thousands'. B, however, covers abuse risk directly with multiple accounts, email or GitHub verification and blocking disposable emails. A barely touches that risk, so B edges ahead overall.
